# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-delivery-timing

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Delivery Timing** in isolation on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash` (`high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter, `$40` cost cap). Non-blocking incoming peer messages are buffered up to 4 steps until a natural workflow boundary (a passing test, git, or pull-request command, a messaging turn, or an exploration-to-editing shift). Compared against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-stepcounter` (4/10 passed, 2 merge conflicts on same-function overlap pairs `dspy_task/8563` and `react_hook_form_task/153`).

## Observations

- Eliminated **all merge conflicts** across all 10 `core` pairs (`0` conflicts: 9 `clean` merges and 1 `identical` branch pair on `typst_task/6554`), including all three same-function overlap pairs (`dspy_task/8563`, `go_chi_task/27`, and `react_hook_form_task/153`), down from 2 conflicts in the `coop --git` baseline.
- Overall pass rate matched the `coop --git` baseline at 4/10 (`dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655`, `openai_tiktoken_task/0`, `pallets_jinja_task/1559`, and `typst_task/6554` — flipping `pallets_jinja_task/1559` from fail to pass while `pallets_jinja_task/1621` flipped from pass to single-feature pass).
- On every one of the 6 non-passing pairs, one of the two features passed cleanly after merging while the peer's feature failed functional assertions, showing that `delivery-timing` solved git integration collisions cleanly while leaving semantic coordination gaps for `intents` to address.
